title: Pneumonia with a creatinine rise that is never named
discharge_summary: SYNTHETIC CASE - NOT A REAL PATIENT
Patient: Synthetic Patient 01, 72-year-old male. MRN: SYN-0001
Reason for admission: Fever, productive cough, and shortness of breath for 3 days.

The patient presented with fever of 38.9 C, cough, and right lower lobe infiltrate on chest x-ray. He was started on IV ceftriaxone and azithromycin for community-acquired pneumonia. Oral intake had been poor for several days before admission.

Creatinine was 2.3 mg/dL on admission; his baseline creatinine is 1.0 mg/dL per clinic records from last month. Urine output was 0.4 mL/kg/hr for the first 12 hours. Metformin and lisinopril were held. He received IV normal saline at 125 mL/hr for 48 hours. Creatinine improved to 1.6 on hospital day 2 and 1.1 at discharge.
Oxygen saturation remained 93-96% on room air throughout the stay.
Blood glucose was well controlled on sliding-scale insulin while metformin was held.
Discharge plan: Oral amoxicillin-clavulanate to complete 7 days. Resume metformin and lisinopril in 48 hours if labs are stable. Repeat basic metabolic panel in 1 week.

expected.notes: Creatinine 2.3 from baseline 1.0 with low urine output, treated with IV fluids and held nephrotoxic meds: indicators of acute kidney injury, which the physician never names. Query for AKI (N17.9, CC).
